entityName: HUN-REN Szamitastechnikai es Automatizalasi Kutato Intezet
entityDescription: SZTAKI is a research institute, governed by the Hungarian Research Network. SZTAKI is the Hungarian acronym for "Institute for Computer Science and Control". The Institute was founded in 1973. Its staff consists of more than 300 full-time employees, more than 200 with university diploma and more than 70 with scientific degrees. The fundamental task of the Institute is to perform basic and application-oriented research in an interdisciplinary setting in the fields of computer science, engineering, information technology, intelligent systems, process control, wide-area networking and multimedia.Contract-based target research, development, training and expert support for domestic and foreign industrial, governmental and other partners are important activities at the Institute.The mission of SZTAKI includes the transfer of up-to-date research results and state-of-the-art technology to university students. The Institute is very active in graduate and postgraduate education, co-operating with most technical universities in Hungary and operating common chairs, postgraduate programs with them. More than 40 members of the Institute¿s researchers conduct regular lectures/classes at graduate and postgraduate levels, and senior researchers hold part-time positions as university professors. 20-30 Ph.D. students and 20-30 graduate students participate in the work of the Institute.

entityName: CZECH UNIVERSITY OF LIFE SCIENCES PRAGUE
entityDescription:
Czech University of Life Sciences Prague (CZU) is a public higher education institution offering study programs at the Bachelor, Master, and Doctoral levels. At present, 20,500 students, including 10,229 females and 5,660 international students, are enrolled in daily and combined forms of study across 297 study programs, with 155 taught entirely in English. CZU employs approximately 1,600 staff members, including more than 800 academic staff, such as professors, associate professors, senior researchers, and lecturers.
Research at CZU focuses on environmental, biological, agricultural, socio-economic, and technical topics, with faculties and departments actively participating in research projects funded by Czech national grant agencies such as the Czech Science Foundation, The National Agency for Agriculture Research, and the Technology Agency of the Czech Republic, as well as international grant agencies such as Horizon Europe, Erasmus, LIFE, COST, and OECD. CZU manages around 400 research projects annually, with approximately one-third being international collaborations. The university is currently implementing up to 50 Horizon Europe projects, further strengthening its role in European research and innovation.
As a leading institution in life sciences, CZU is an active member of several prestigious international organizations, including the Euroleague for Life Sciences (ELLS), the Association for European Life Science Universities (ICA), the Danube Rector’s Conference (DRC), the Central and South Eastern Europe ICA Regional Network (CASEE), AGRINATURA – The European Alliance on Agricultural Knowledge for Development, and the European University Association (EUA).
CZU maintains a gender-balanced environment in accordance with EU requirements, as established in its Gender Equality Plan (GEP) and supported by the HR Award, ensuring an inclusive and diverse academic and research environment.

entityDescription:
The UCO is heir to a centuries-old historical and cultural legacy as well as a passion for knowledge, tolerance, international renown and harmony among civilizations that have made the city that houses our institution a paradigm for humanity. This equilibrium and harmony is reflected in the three areas in which the UCO undertakes its activities: Food and Agriculture and Science and Technology; Humanities and the Legal and Social Sciences; and the Health Sciences; each with its own special characteristics. This balance is also manifested in quality teaching and research, ranking it among the top academic institutions in Spain.

The UCO is one of the foremost research institutions in Spain; a distinction that will be further consolidated with the creation of the Rabanales 21 Science and Technology Park and the Maimonides Institute for Biomedical Research. Our university is an international leader in the agrifood field, one of the institution¿s main vocations; not to overlook the importance of the humanities in a city that is known throughout the world for its artistic and monumental heritage.

A young, dynamic university dedicated to research and in constant evolution, the UCO is firmly committed to the problems and needs of the community at large. As a public institution, it connects closely with the society it serves, but is also dedicated to aiding other peoples and countries. The UCO maintains strong ties with business and other entities, while also structuring much of its own activity around an entrepreneurial vision. Most importantly, it is an institution that is not only committed to training qualified professionals, but to supporting and encouraging its students to grow as people and as citizens.

entityDescription: Łukasiewicz Research Network - Krakow Institute of Technology (in Polish: Sieć Badawcza Łukasiewicz - Krakowski Instytut Technologiczny) was established on April 1, 2020 as a result of the merger of two Krakow institutes included in the Łukasiewicz Research Network: the Foundry Research Institute and the Institute of Advanced Manufacturing Technologies. Together, the two institutes, with decades of tradition and experience, have created a strong unit capable of taking on new challenges in development directions crucial for the Łukasiewicz Research Network, i.e. health, intelligent mobility, sustainable economy and energy, and digital transformation of strategic importance for the Polish economy. The headquarters of Łukasiewicz - Krakow Institute of Technology is located at ul. Zakopiańska 73. The Institute employs 208 employees, including research department employees, engineers and support department employees. The Institute has specialized equipment for conducting research on a laboratory scale as well as on a semi-industrial scale. There are four Centers in the structure: the Center for Casting Technology, the Center for Advanced Manufacturing Technologies, the Material Processing Center and the Material Research Center, in which the key team of the research department responsible for generating innovative solutions for the Polish economy is concentrated. The recipients of solutions developed at the Institute are representatives of the foundry, tooling, aviation, medical, energy and many other industries. The Institute also offers commercial services carried out mainly at the Center of Research Laboratories (including Accredited Laboratories), as well as by the Certification and Standardization Bureau. The Institute also has a production department focusing on the design and manufacture of production lines for the packaging industry. Łukasiewicz - Kraków Institute of Technology conducts interdisciplinary research covering both classical and modern technologies of material production and processing. The Institute develops 3D printing technologies based on metals, plastics and ceramics, and also manufactures materials and tools for the advanced technology industry. Other research areas of the Institute include the design and manufacture of materials for electromobility, including fuel cells, the production and processing of composite and nanocomposite materials for special applications, and the development of robotization and automation of processes in line with the assumptions of Industry 4.0. In the near future, scientists of the Łukasiewicz - Krakow Institute of Technology will also undertake work in the field of designing material solutions and production technology for the renewable energy industry, including offshore wind energy and the domestic photovoltaic sector, and the corrosion research area will be expanded to include biocorrosion and corrosion in the chloride environment. The high level of work carried out at the Institute guarantees cooperation with numerous scientific and research centers in the world, including joint research projects, participation in scientific conferences, exchange of personnel and valuable experience in the field of research and implementation.

Company description: Łukasiewicz Research Network - Krakow Institute of Technology (in Polish: Sieć Badawcza Łukasiewicz - Krakowski Instytut Technologiczny) was established on April 1, 2020 as a result of the merger of two Krakow institutes included in the Łukasiewicz Research Network: the Foundry Research Institute and the Institute of Advanced Manufacturing Technologies. Together, the two institutes, with decades of tradition and experience, have created a strong unit capable of taking on new challenges in development directions crucial for the Łukasiewicz Research Network, i.e. health, intelligent mobility, sustainable economy and energy, and digital transformation of strategic importance for the Polish economy. The headquarters of Łukasiewicz - Krakow Institute of Technology is located at ul. Zakopiańska 73. The Institute employs 208 employees, including research department employees, engineers and support department employees. The Institute has specialized equipment for conducting research on a laboratory scale as well as on a semi-industrial scale. There are four Centers in the structure: the Center for Casting Technology, the Center for Advanced Manufacturing Technologies, the Material Processing Center and the Material Research Center, in which the key team of the research department responsible for generating innovative solutions for the Polish economy is concentrated. The recipients of solutions developed at the Institute are representatives of the foundry, tooling, aviation, medical, energy and many other industries. The Institute also offers commercial services carried out mainly at the Center of Research Laboratories (including Accredited Laboratories), as well as by the Certification and Standardization Bureau. The Institute also has a production department focusing on the design and manufacture of production lines for the packaging industry. Łukasiewicz - Kraków Institute of Technology conducts interdisciplinary research covering both classical and modern technologies of material production and processing. The Institute develops 3D printing technologies based on metals, plastics and ceramics, and also manufactures materials and tools for the advanced technology industry. Other research areas of the Institute include the design and manufacture of materials for electromobility, including fuel cells, the production and processing of composite and nanocomposite materials for special applications, and the development of robotization and automation of processes in line with the assumptions of Industry 4.0. In the near future, scientists of the Łukasiewicz - Krakow Institute of Technology will also undertake work in the field of designing material solutions and production technology for the renewable energy industry, including offshore wind energy and the domestic photovoltaic sector, and the corrosion research area will be expanded to include biocorrosion and corrosion in the chloride environment. The high level of work carried out at the Institute guarantees cooperation with numerous scientific and research centers in the world, including joint research projects, participation in scientific conferences, exchange of personnel and valuable experience in the field of research and implementation.

entityDescription:
Hertz Systems has been operating for over 34 years (including ownership transformations) providing end to end solutions – from design to manufacturing, assembly, integration, testing and training. We provide hardware and software solutions for the military, government and European institutions, and the as well as private sector. Hertz Systems is located in western part of Poland (Zielona Góra, close to Berlin).
For almost 20 years the company has been active on the military market developing satellite navigation receivers integrated with crypto modules. Hertz Systems devices are dedicated for various combat vehicles and other military platforms requiring precise and reliable PVT. More than 2,000 of our receivers have been delivered to the Polish Armed Forces. Work is currently underway on receivers integrated with M-Code and GALILEO modules.
Hertz Systems also executes space projects related to, among others, GNSS systems for downstream applications as well as sensors for space. The entity holds Security Accreditation Board authorization to access PRS technology and aims to manufacture PRS receivers in Poland. Furthermore, the entity provides testing and validation services for satellite modules, it is also equipped with SimPRS software enabling generation of real PRS signals.
Hertz Systems also specializes in systems ensuring safety of critical infrastructure (Hawk system for detection and neutralization of drones) and critical data (TEMPEST equipment). The aim of the Hawk system is to detect the drone before invading the protected area, track it in real time and bring it to the ground or neutralize it in the air. The system generates and automatic alert in the event of intrusion into the guarded zone and effectively neutralizes the intruder.
The company declares its expertise in project management at all TRL levels and project phases (from design through manufacturing till market introduction), practical knowledge in software and hardware for GNSS applications, access to Electromagnetic Compatibility Laboratory and professional equipment/software.
Hertz Systems is a highly trusted partner, which is confirmed by various licenses and certificates. Implemented Quality Management System complies with standards of PN EN ISO 9001 and AQAP 2110 and 2210. Moreover, the company holds Concession, issued by the Ministry of the Interior and Administration for manufacturing and sales of products and technology dedicated for military and police use. 
Hertz Systems has its own, in-house R&D department located in Science and Technology Park close to company HQ.

entityDescription: Ciência Viva, created in 1996, is the National Agency for the promotion of scientific culture and technology. It is a non-profit association and its members are national research laboratories and science policy institutes. Its main goal is to promote public awareness of Science and Technology among the general public, with a particular focus on young people. To reach this goal, Ciência Viva develops its activities along three strategic axes: a) Science education (teacher training, science projects for schools, summer internships for secondary school students in research centres and institutions); b) Science communication events for the general public (Science in Summer, Science and Technology Week, World Space Week, talks and debates); c) A national network of Ciência Viva Science Centres, in collaboration with local authorities and universities. Presently there are 20 Ciência Viva Science Centres nationwide. Ciência Viva has been actively promoting, supporting and developing science education activities in the area of Space Science and Technology since 1999 and has been an active promoter of ESA¿s educational projects since then. These activities and projects include the development of projects with schools (e.g. participation in ESA¿s project ¿Greenhouse in Space¿, and ¿Astrobiology: other worlds, other lives? - 2010/2011, and ¿Mission-X¿ ¿ 2011/2012), the yearly coordination and dissemination of the World Space Week, the organization and coordination of Astronomy in Summer, a national campaign of astronomical observations and activities and the organization of talks and debates. Over the last years, the Ciência Viva Science Centre Network has gained considerable experience in training through teacher development courses organised in the centres that are already certified as teacher training centres. Participation in the European projects Fibonacci, Pollen and SciencEduc, amongst others, has also strongly enriched Ciência Viva¿s experience.

entityDescription:
G & A Engineering S.r.l. is a small company operating for over 45 years in military and space sector.
The company is located in a modern plant in Oricola (AQ), in a land of 18,000 square meters, divided into different buildings and structured to meet the needs arising from research, design, engineering, experimentation, prototyping and series construction, that the company carries out in military, space, industrial, medical and professional sectors.
The company has several workshops with tools, machines and equipment of the latest generation that, together with the company know-how and qualified and multidisciplinary staff, have allowed to consolidate high-level technologies and processes that allow it to operate in sectors very challenging and that make it independent in passing from an idea to a finished product.
The company workshop includes: Microelectronic Workshop, Metrologic Workshop, Electronic Workshop with Laboratory Instrumentation, Mechanic Workshop.
Over the years the company has consolidated high-level technologies, processes and know-how that allow to operate in very challenging sectors and has a structure that guarantees the sale of services/products at all stages of their "Life Cycle", carrying out research, design, engineering, industrialization, manufacturing and logistics activities, integrated with the continuous application of all the standards typical of space, military and industrial sectors. Unique and peculiar characteristic of the Company is the ability to design and build "Special Equipment", ie custom designed devices built with criteria that make a prototype comparable, for finishes and construction features, with an industrialized product; these special equipment typically include electronic, microelectronic and electrical technologies as well as mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic, vacuum, etc ...; beyond that, the company is known on the market for its ability to cooperate with the world of research and the ability to make experimental systems indistinguishable from industrial systems.

entityDescription:
Starlab
converts science into technologies with a profound positive impact on society
and the planet. Scientists, engineers and economists from different
nationalities work together with a common goal: to provide our clients with
breakthrough technologies that create business opportunities.

As
market-oriented scientists, we believe that the potential for innovation is
greater when we rethink the basics together with our clients. We build on
scientific research and sound engineering to deliver cutting edge solutions.

We are
experts in the development of instrumentation and information processing
systems: from sensors to algorithms to applications and the development of
information efficient models.

Our main
areas of work lie in the space and applied neuroscience sectors.

Space Engineering Business Unit

On the
technology side, Starlab is working today on the development of new space
sensors and mission concepts for environmental monitoring, including remote
sensing applications of GPS and Galileo, as well as new radar concepts. On the
application side, we develop and continue to improve operational information
services using space data for oil spill monitoring and water quality.

Neuroscience Research Business Unit

Starlab
Neuroscience Research develops applications and smart systems with a focus on
electrophysiology and computational intelligence in the fields of medicine,
neuromodulation, human machine interaction, assistive technology, safety and
biometry.

entityDescription: DFRC iis a high-tech SME located in Zug, with its research centre in Bern, Switzerland. DFRC is a leading centre of knowledge, research and development of geospatial data fusion and analysis. DFRC's patent protected technology focuses on understanding the behaviour of real-world objects using sparse observations sets. Based on this technology DFRC has developed two main business lines: (i)service WWAIS: creating situation awarness pictures and detecting abnormal behaviours in maritime traffic; (ii)using DFRC's own sensors fused with other data, creating situation awarness pictures and trend analysis within crowds and city flows.
